lines.trans: Hi, Vitya, do you need fresh fish from Japan?
Wait, that is poisonous fugu fish!
I will give it to you for half the price.
No, Timur, take it back with you.
Oguzok, why are you late for your shift again?
Actually, Chef, the critic liked my pâté.
It was because of me that we were mentioned in the guide.
Maybe he simply liked the bread or the water?
You say that because you are jealous of me.

examples.text: Может, ты придёшь потом, после меня?
examples.trans: Maybe you can come back later, after me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А вы думали, что от меня избавились?
examples.trans: And did you think that you had gotten rid of me?

examples.text: Что, шеф, на большие деньги повелись?
examples.trans: Well, Chef, did you fall for the big money?

examples.text: Прости, что я тебе тогда не сказала.
examples.trans: Forgive me for not telling you back then.

завидовать.gloss: to envy, to be jealous of

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'видовать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to envy, to be jealous of', paired with 'позавидовать'.

examples.text: Все мальчишки завидовали ему.
examples.trans: All the boys envied him.

examples.text: Я тебе по-хорошему завидую.
examples.trans: I envy you in a good way.

examples.text: У него было ружьё. Все мальчишки завидовали ему.
examples.trans: He had an air gun. All the boys envied him.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to decide; to solve', paired with 'решать'.

examples.text: Ты решил, что готовишь лучше меня?
examples.trans: Have you decided that you cook better than me?

examples.text: Суд решил.
examples.trans: The court has decided.

examples.text: Я решил.
examples.trans: I've decided.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'cook', paired with 'приготовить'.

examples.text: Ты решил, что готовишь лучше меня?
examples.trans: Have you decided that you cook better than me?

examples.text: Если ты лучше меня, ты приготовишь фугу.
examples.trans: If you are better than me, you will prepare fugu.

examples.text: Конечно, я знаю, что там готовить.
examples.trans: Of course I know what there is to cook.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'better', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сегодня самый лучший день в моей жизни.
examples.trans: Today is the very best day of my life.

examples.text: Ты решил, что готовишь лучше меня?
examples.trans: Have you decided that you cook better than me?

examples.text: Если ты лучше меня, ты приготовишь фугу.
examples.trans: If you are better than me, you will prepare fugu.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Тогда быстро за работу, бездельники!
examples.trans: Then get back to work quickly, slackers!

examples.text: Прости, что я тебе тогда не сказала.
examples.trans: Forgive me for not telling you back then.

examples.text: Тогда я предлагаю тебе честное пари.
examples.trans: Then I propose an honest bet to you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'лагать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning '(I) suggest', paired with 'предложить'.

examples.text: Тогда я предлагаю тебе честное пари.
examples.trans: Then I propose an honest bet to you.

examples.text: Тогда предлагаю тебе пари.
examples.trans: Then I propose a bet to you.

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, предлагаю вам первым оценить блюдо.
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich, I invite you to evaluate the dish first.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('honest').

examples.text: Честное слово, она улыбнулась, я не вру!
examples.trans: Honestly, she smiled, I am not lying!

examples.text: Тогда я предлагаю тебе честное пари.
examples.trans: Then I propose an honest bet to you.

examples.text: Честное слово, я сплетни не распространяю.
examples.trans: Honestly, I am not spreading gossip.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'bet, wager' in everyday Russian.

related.gloss: to steam oneself in a bathhouse

examples.text: Тогда я предлагаю тебе честное пари.
examples.trans: Then I propose an honest bet to you.

examples.text: Тогда предлагаю тебе пари.
examples.trans: Then I propose a bet to you.

examples.text: Это же пари, вдруг вы сами не умеете?
examples.trans: It is a bet, what if you do not know how yourself?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если ты лучше меня, ты приготовишь фугу.
examples.trans: If you are better than me, you will prepare fugu.

examples.text: Если останешься жив, признаю, что ты лучше.
examples.trans: If you stay alive, I will admit you are better.

examples.text: Подумай, сколько ты сэкономишь, если подпишешь его сейчас.
examples.trans: Think how much you will save if you sign him now.

meanings.en: to cook, to make (food), to prepare
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will prepare', paired with 'готовить'.

examples.text: Если ты лучше меня, ты приготовишь фугу.
examples.trans: If you are better than me, you will prepare fugu.

examples.text: Ты её сам приготовишь и сам съешь.
examples.trans: You will prepare it yourself and eat it yourself.

examples.text: Давай мы с тобой по половине приготовим.
examples.trans: Let's each prepare half of the fish.
